Here’s a concise, practical overview of the International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders (IJLCD).

What it is
- A leading peer‑reviewed journal for research on human communication and swallowing across the lifespan, with strong clinical and applied focus for speech and language therapy/pathology.
- Official journal of the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists (RCSLT).
- Published by Wiley (John Wiley & Sons) on behalf of RCSLT.
- Current title adopted in 1997; the journal was previously the British Journal of Disorders of Communication (established in the 1960s).

Scope and typical topics
- Assessment, diagnosis, intervention, and outcomes in speech, language, communication, and swallowing.
- Populations: children and adults; developmental and acquired disorders (e.g., DLD, stuttering, autism, aphasia, dysarthria, apraxia, voice disorders, dysphagia).
- Settings: health, education, community, acute and rehabilitation.
- Methods: experimental, clinical trials, observational/epidemiological, qualitative and mixed‑methods, psychometrics, implementation science, service delivery and policy, technology and AAC.
- Strong emphasis on clinical relevance and implications for practice.

Audience
- Researchers and clinicians in speech and language therapy/pathology, linguistics, psychology, education, audiology, neurology, rehabilitation, and public health.

Editorial and publication model
- Publisher: Wiley; Society: RCSLT.
- Frequency: generally six issues per year (bimonthly).
- Peer review: external, single‑blind (authors’ identities known to reviewers; reviewers anonymous) is typical for Wiley health science titles; special issues may vary.
- Official language: English.
- Online submission and tracking (Wiley’s ScholarOne Manuscripts platform).

Indexing and discoverability
- Indexed in major databases commonly used in the field, including MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Clarivate’s Web of Science (Social Sciences Citation Index). Also typically covered in PsycINFO and CINAHL.
- Impact/metrics: the journal’s Journal Impact Factor has recently been in the low‑to‑mid range for clinical communication sciences; current figures change annually—check the Wiley journal homepage or Journal Citation Reports for the latest number. CiteScore and H‑index are available via Scopus.

Open access and archiving
- Hybrid open access: authors can publish either subscription (no APC) or open access for a fee.
- APC: Wiley’s hybrid APCs are typically in the low‑to‑mid‑$3000s USD; exact fee, currency options, and tax status are listed on the journal’s “Open Access” page.
- Many institutions have Wiley transformative agreements that can cover or discount APCs for corresponding authors.
- Copyright: standard Wiley license for subscription articles; open access options usually include Creative Commons licenses (often CC BY or CC BY‑NC).
- Archiving: authors can usually deposit accepted manuscripts in repositories after an embargo per Wiley’s self‑archiving policy; check the journal’s “Author Guidelines” for specifics.
- Data and materials: Wiley journals require a Data Availability Statement and encourage FAIR sharing; clinical datasets may need de‑identification and controlled access.

Article types you’ll commonly see
- Original research articles (quantitative, qualitative, mixed‑methods)
- Systematic reviews, scoping reviews, meta‑analyses
- Methodological papers, measurement/validation studies
- Brief reports or short communications
- Clinical forums, commentaries, and letters
- Protocols (occasionally; check current policy)
- Many papers include required “What this paper adds” or “Clinical implications”/Key Points sections to enhance practice relevance.

Submission basics (always verify current instructions)
- Structured abstracts are standard; word limits vary by article type.
- Style: APA‑style citations/reference formatting are commonly required.
- Reporting guidelines: PRISMA for reviews, CONSORT for trials, STROBE for observational studies, COREQ for qualitative, etc. EQUATOR Network compliance is encouraged/required.
- Ethics: confirmation of IRB/ethics approval and informed consent where applicable; clinical trials should be prospectively registered.
- Suggested reviewers may be requested; conflicts of interest and funding statements are mandatory.

Timelines and acceptance rate
- Time to first decision and acceptance rates fluctuate by year and submission type. In recent years, first decisions for many Wiley clinical titles often fall in the 4–10 week range, but IJLCD’s exact median can differ. Check the journal’s homepage or recent editorials for up‑to‑date metrics.

Accessing content
- Website: hosted on Wiley Online Library (search “International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders Wiley”).
- Many articles are open via OA or become free after an interval; society members (RCSLT) typically have access benefits.

Identifiers
- Print ISSN: 1368‑2822
- Online ISSN: 1460‑6984

Tips if you’re considering submitting
- Align your study with clear clinical implications and include a succinct “What this paper adds” section if requested.
- Use robust, field‑standard outcome measures; report effect sizes and confidence intervals.
- For intervention studies, describe treatment fidelity, dosage, and replicability; for single‑case designs, use recognized reporting standards.
- Provide transparent data and code sharing where ethically feasible.
- Pre‑submission inquiries are welcome for borderline‑scope topics or special issues.

If you want, I can:
- Link you to the current Author Guidelines and Open Access/APC page.
- Check whether your topic fits the journal’s recent special issues or calls for papers.
- Review a draft abstract for scope fit and clarity.
